_why: The curated half of 'the neighbourhood of the word' (src/medical/term_lookup.py). When a radiologist highlights a term, the service shows terms that look like it (spelling, from radiology_lexicon.txt) and terms that go with it (this file, plus stem families mined from the lexicon). Stems find pneumothorax -> haemothorax for free; only a human can say pneumothorax -> chest drain. That is what belongs here.
_how_to_extend: Add a term to an existing group, or add a new group. A group is a set of terms that belong together clinically; every member is offered as a neighbour of every other member, so no pair has to be written twice. Terms may be phrases ('chest drain') and need not be in the lexicon. Two rules: keep groups small (a 30-term group makes every one of its members a weak suggestion), and put first the members a shared stem could never find — only the first few of a group are shown before the mined stems, and writing 'haemothorax' under 'pneumothorax' spends that space on something the stems already produce.
_not_clinical_guidance: These are associative hints for finding a word, never a differential diagnosis and never advice. Nothing here is applied to the report automatically.

tuning._why: Knobs live here rather than in the code that reads them. min_morpheme_chars is the one worth understanding: at 4 the mined stems start matching grammar rather than meaning (fracture -> echotexture on '-ture', meniscus -> meningioma on 'meni-'); 5 keeps '-thorax', 'pneumo-' and '-ectasis' and drops those.
